business_problem: After unifying its core data estate, PayPal needed an AI platform that could power global commerce use cases, let developers choose the best model for each workload, and elastically handle training and inference without reverting to monolithic release cycles or custom infrastructure for every project.
solution_summary: PayPal built its next-generation AI stack on Google Cloud by combining BigQuery, Google Kubernetes Engine, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Cloud GPUs into a unified model and infrastructure layer. BigQuery provides the AI-ready data foundation following PayPal's migration of more than 300 petabytes, while GKE gives teams an elastic architecture that replaced slower monolithic release patterns and now supports 25,000 pipelines per day. On top of that runtime, PayPal created a unified LLM stack: open-source models run on the GKE inferencing layer, while proprietary models such as Gemini run through Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and Model Garden. Cloud GPU capacity provides the compute horsepower for training and high-performance workloads. This architecture lets developers move from idea to production quickly while preserving security, compliance, and model-choice flexibility across PayPal's 439 million-user commerce business.

solution_components.name: BigQuery
solution_components.role: Stores the unified data foundation that PayPal uses to train, evaluate, and operationalize AI workloads at global scale.

solution_components.name: Google Kubernetes Engine
solution_components.role: Runs the elastic inferencing and application architecture that replaced slower monolithic release patterns.

solution_components.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
solution_components.role: Hosts proprietary model access and gives developers a governed path to production AI agents and Model Garden assets.

solution_components.name: Cloud GPUs
solution_components.role: Provide the high-performance training and inference compute needed for PayPal's unified AI stack.

data_flow: Enterprise data lands in BigQuery and is consumed by PayPal's data scientists and AI services. Open-source models run on the GKE inferencing layer, proprietary models such as Gemini are served through Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Cloud GPUs supply the training and inference capacity needed to scale AI products into commerce workflows.
business_outcome: PayPal transformed its post-migration data estate into a flexible AI platform that speeds releases, supports tens of thousands of pipelines a day, and lets the business scale agentic commerce capabilities without locking teams into a single model vendor or architecture pattern.
